name: LOWER STREET
materialIdentity: Wooden false fronts on a wide mud street at night, Main Street's palette further along: the Registrar's lit window, the white church, the livery's open doors (errata 161)
note: Room 43, errata 43's Room 2b: Main Street's east end through the receding road. Built at errata 161 (Tyler: "Lower Street and the Lane"). Lines EXTRACTED from doc 97 by tools/extract-examine.mjs and compiled by tools/compile-room.mjs from reference/room-43/annotation.json.

repeat: Lamplight through old glass, gone wavy with age. Even the window has been made to wait.
The lamp is always lit. I have never seen anyone trim it. I suspect it is filed.
then: Somewhere behind the glare is a man who has never once been surprised.

LISTEN_TO.say: A pen, scratching, then a long pause, then a stamp.
repeat: A page turning, very slowly. Somewhere in there a claim is being read to the last comma.
The stamp again. It is the most decisive sound in Consolation.
then: The rhythm of a form being found incomplete.

overrides.OPEN: It doesn't open. The Registrar's business is done through the door, in the order received.

LOOK_AT.say: A water trough with a skin of dust on it and a square of night sky in the middle.
repeat: Horses drink from it, dogs drink from it, and one man, I suspect, late on Saturdays.
Planks, pitch and iron bands. It holds water the way this town holds a grudge: completely.

LISTEN_TO.say: A slow drip from the seam, keeping its own time.
repeat: Nothing. Still water, minding its business.
A moth on the surface, rowing for shore.

overrides.USE: I washed my face in it. Now I'm dusty and wet, which out here passes for clean.

LOOK_AT.say: A bell on a post by the church steps, with a dent where the mallet lands.
repeat: Brass, gone green at the rim. Somebody polishes the dent and nothing else.
You can't tune a bell, not properly. I could still have a long talk with it.
then: It was cast to a note, and it has been coming down off it ever since.

LISTEN_TO.say: It hums when the wind catches it. Even humming, it's low.
repeat: I flicked it with a fingernail. Half a step flat, and comfortable there.
Nothing now. It's resting between insults to the scale.

overrides.TALK_TO: I told it it was flat. It took it better than most of the people I've told things to here.
overrides.USE: Not without the mallet, and not without the man who owns the mallet, and ideally not at all.

LOOK_AT.say: The livery stable. The doors stand open on a lantern and a heap of hay.
repeat: A hay loft over the doors, shut tight, as though the hay might make a run for it.
I could hire a horse, if I had the price of a horse's afternoon. I have about the price of its nap.
then: The horses are further in, out of sight and, from the sound of them, out of patience.

LISTEN_TO.say: Horses, shifting their weight and their opinions.
repeat: A long, judgmental snort. I'm choosing to believe it was aimed at the street in general.
A bucket set down, and a horse investigating it.

LOOK_AT.say: The church, which on weekdays is the meeting hall and on most days is neither.
repeat: The steps up to the doors. One has been replaced; the rest have been worn smooth by people arriving in a hurry and leaving slowly.
The belfry has a bell of its own, rung from inside on a rope. Out here the ringing is done by hand, from the post, at whatever hour the ringer feels it.
then: The whitest thing in town, because it is the only thing anyone repaints.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing from inside. The pews are holding their breath for Sunday.
repeat: The doors, ticking as the night cools them. Even the church settles.
Somewhere inside, a hymnal falling shut. Nobody there to have been reading it.

overrides.TALK_TO: I said a short word for my claim. It was received the way the Registrar receives things: in silence, and filed.

LOOK_AT.say: Main Street's mud, continued. Out here it has stopped trying to impress anyone.
repeat: Wheel ruts, swinging wide around the corner. Every wagon in town takes it the long way, out of respect.
The far end of town. In Providence this is where the better houses would be. Here it is where the street gives up and becomes a road.

LISTEN_TO.say: Quieter than Main Street. The piano is a rumor from here.
repeat: Hooves in the livery, and the mud settling after them.
A dog, two streets over, objecting to something on principle.

overrides.PICK_UP: Lower Street's mud is Main Street's, only less looked at. I'll leave it its privacy.

exits.name: THE ROAD BACK TO MAIN STREET

LOOK_AT.say: The road back up to Main Street, where the lamps are closer together and the mud is better dressed.
repeat: The lights get thicker that way. So does the queue.
Lower Street is where Main Street keeps the things it needs and doesn't like to look at: the law, the church, the horses, and me.

LISTEN_TO.say: Main Street, a little way off. The Nugget, mostly.
repeat: Boots on boardwalks up there, and nothing down here but mud being patient.
A door banging up on Main Street, and the whole street turning to look. I can hear it turning.

exits.note: Errata 43: west, back along the receding road to Main Street's east end.

exits.name: THE REGISTRAR'S DOOR

LOOK_AT.say: The Claims Registrar's, with a light in the window every time I have walked past. The paperwork does not sleep.
repeat: Two steps up to the door, worn hollow in the middle by four thousand men going in hopeful.
A plain door. It's the only plain thing about the business done behind it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Through the door, a stamp, then a pen, then the stamp again.
repeat: The bell on the door inside, settling after the last man out.
Nobody on the step. Whoever is waiting is inside, keeping warm.

exits.note: Errata 43: the Claims Registrar opens off Lower Street.

exits.name: THE ALLEY

LOOK_AT.say: A gap between the Registrar's and the church, going round the back of everything.
repeat: Every town has a way round the back of itself. This one goes past the barrels to the watchman's door.
It's narrow enough that two men meeting in it would have to agree on something.

LISTEN_TO.say: The alley, breathing cold air out between the buildings.
repeat: A cat in there somewhere, saying something definite.
Barrels, knocking hollow when the wind gets behind them.

exits.note: Errata 43: Room 20, the back alley, opens off Lower Street.

exits.name: THE CHURCH DOORS

LOOK_AT.say: Double doors up the steps, and a bell hung on a post beside them, at a height for ringing by hand.
repeat: The paint is fresher than anything else on Lower Street. Sowerby takes a collection for it, and for the doors, and for the steps.
The bell on its post is half a step flat. I've told nobody. It isn't the kind of thing a church wants to hear.

LISTEN_TO.say: Inside, a hymnal's pages turning, or the draft turning them for nobody.
repeat: The bell on its post humming very faintly when the wind catches it. Flat, even humming.
The doors creaking in their frame, the way church doors do, as though they had been asked a question.

exits.note: Errata 43: the church and meeting hall.

exits.name: THE PASSAGE TO THE LANE

LOOK_AT.say: A passage through to the Lane, where the undertaker and the medium keep each other in business.
repeat: Dark, short and mostly mud. The Lane at the other end is lit better than you'd expect, for what's in it.
Narrow enough to make a man walk sideways if anyone is coming the other way, and on the Lane someone generally is.

LISTEN_TO.say: Small bells, from the far end: the tent flap, letting somebody out.
repeat: A plane on wood, faint and patient. The undertaker, getting ahead.
The draft through the gap, carrying the Lane's quiet out into the street.

exits.note: Errata 43: the Lane connects through to Lower Street at its far end.

LOOK_AT.say: The livery's doors, open a man's width, with a lamp inside and straw spilling out to meet the mud.
repeat: A trough beside them for anyone who arrives on four legs, and nothing for anyone on two, which seems about right for a livery.
Somewhere in there is a mule with opinions. From out here the stable looks very peaceful about it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Hooves shifting on straw, and a mule saying something short.
repeat: The lamp inside, hissing, and a mule breathing near it.
The trough dripping at one corner. It has dripped there a long time; the mud under it is a different color.

exits.name: THE ROAD OUT OF TOWN

LOOK_AT.say: The road out of town, to the claims. Every man in Consolation walks it in the morning and back at night, and only the mornings are hopeful.
repeat: A fence runs beside it a little way and then gives up, which is where the town ends and the diggings begin.
By day it's the miners' road. At night it belongs to whoever is still walking it.

LISTEN_TO.say: The wind coming down from the diggings, with a loose board knocking somewhere along the way.
repeat: The lamp on the post by the fence, hissing to itself.
Far off, a dog at a claim. Even the dogs have boundaries out there.

exits.note: Errata 161: the road out to the claims, which Main Street's east road was before.

entrances.note: In along the road from Main Street, at left.
Out of the passage from the Lane.
In along the road from the claims, at right.

PICK_UP.say: I am not going to pick up the bell-ringer. He is the only thing holding the bell up, morally.

PUSH.say: He sways enough on his own. I'm not going to add a vote.

USE.say: He has one use, and he is already putting it to work, half a step flat.

lamps.note: The stable's lamplight through the open doors.
